title: The Unreliable Narrator
text:
In many nineteenth-century novels, the narrator is presented as a trustworthy guide to the events of the story. Critics have long observed, however, that some narrators conceal their own motives, and the reader must gradually discern what has been left unsaid. Analysing such texts requires attention not only to what is described but also to the gaps, hesitations and selective emphases in the narration.

The technique is sometimes called the unreliable narrator, a term popularised by Wayne C. Booth in his 1961 study The Rhetoric of Fiction. Booth argued that a narrator's distortions can be detected when their judgements conflict with the evidence the text provides. Such irony rewards the careful reader, who is invited to become an active interpreter rather than a passive recipient.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must the reader do when a narrator conceals their motives?
options: Accept the narrator's account as reliable
Gradually discern what has been left unsaid
Ignore the gaps in the narration

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, when can a narrator's distortions be detected?
options: When the narrator speaks in the first person
When their judgements conflict with the evidence the text provides
When the author states the error directly
When the novel is read aloud

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of the careful reader?
options: They should trust the narrator completely
They are expected to interpret actively rather than accept the narration passively
They are unnecessary to the meaning of the novel
They should skip the narrator's hesitations

questions.text: The passage implies that a reader who accepts the narrator's account without question would most likely:
options: Become more sceptical of the author
Discover the narrator's hidden motives immediately
Miss the irony and distortions the text contains
Appreciate the novel's historical accuracy more

vocabulary.definition: not able to be trusted to give an accurate account
to hide something so that it is not seen or known
changes that make something untrue or inaccurate
a situation or statement where the meaning is the opposite of what is expected

paragraph_translations: W wielu powieściach dziewiętnastowiecznych narrator przedstawiany jest jako godny zaufania przewodnik po wydarzeniach opowieści. Krytycy od dawna zauważali jednak, że niektórzy narratorzy ukrywają własne motywy, a czytelnik musi stopniowo odkrywać to, co pozostało niewypowiedziane. Analiza takich tekstów wymaga uwagi nie tylko na to, co zostało opisane, lecz także na luki, wahania i selektywne akcenty narracji.

Ta technika bywa nazywana niewiarygodnym narratorem, terminem spopularyzowanym przez Wayne'a C. Bootha w jego studium The Rhetoric of Fiction z 1961 roku. Booth twierdził, że zniekształcenia narratora można wykryć wtedy, gdy jego sądy są sprzeczne z dowodami, które dostarcza tekst. Taka ironia nagradza uważnego czytelnika, który zostaje zaproszony do roli aktywnego interpretatora, a nie biernego odbiorcy.
